questions.stem: The famous Brihadisvara (Rajarajesvaram) temple at Thanjavur was built by which Chola king?
questions.explanation: Rajaraja I (r. 985-1014) built the Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. His son Rajendra I expanded the empire across South-East Asia and built the Gangaikonda Cholapuram. Vijayalaya founded the dynasty around 850. Kulottunga I merged the Chola and Chalukya lineages. The Cholas are known for their maritime reach — their navy raided Srivijaya (modern Sumatra) in 1025.

questions.stem: The Pandya kingdom of ancient Tamilakam had its capital at:
questions.explanation: The Pandyas ruled from Madurai — the famous Tamil Sangams (assemblies of poets) were held under their patronage in the early centuries CE. Kanchipuram was the Pallava capital; Thanjavur was Chola territory; Karur / Vanchi was the Chera capital. Megasthenes (c. 300 BCE) mentions the Pandyas. The Meenakshi temple at Madurai was largely expanded by later Pandyas and Nayaks.

questions.stem: Match the southern dynasty with its capital. A. Cholas (imperial). B. Pallavas. C. Cheras. D. Satavahanas. List-II: 1. Thanjavur, 2. Kanchipuram, 3. Vanchi (Karur), 4. Pratishthana (Paithan).
questions.explanation: Cholas — Thanjavur (later also Gangaikonda Cholapuram). Pallavas — Kanchipuram, today in Tamil Nadu. Cheras — Vanchi / Karur (modern Kerala and western TN). Satavahanas — Pratishthana / Paithan in modern Maharashtra — the dominant power in the Deccan from ~1st century BCE to 3rd century CE. Other key southern capitals — Badami (Chalukyas), Mahabalipuram (coastal Pallava port).

questions.stem: The rock-cut temples at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site — were built by the:
questions.explanation: Mamallapuram's rock-cut Rathas, Shore Temple and the 'Descent of the Ganges' relief were commissioned under the Pallava rulers Narasimhavarman I ('Mamalla', r. 630-668) and his successors. Kanchipuram's Kailasanatha temple (built by Rajasimha) is another major Pallava monument. UNESCO WHS since 1984.

questions.stem: The Satavahana dynasty, which dominated the Deccan in the early centuries of the common era, had its greatest ruler in:
questions.explanation: Gautamiputra Satakarni (r. c. 78-102 CE) — the most celebrated Satavahana ruler; he defeated the Shakas and recovered the dynasty's position. The Nasik prashasti of his mother Gautami Balashri records his victories. Simuka founded the line around 230 BCE. Kanishka was a Kushan (not Satavahana). Rudradaman I was a Shaka ruler (Junagadh Rock Inscription) and a rival of the Satavahanas.

questions.stem: The Chola king who sent a naval expedition to South-East Asia (1025 CE) against the maritime kingdom of Srivijaya (modern Sumatra) was:
questions.explanation: Rajendra I (r. 1014-44) — son of Rajaraja I — led the famous naval expedition against Srivijaya in 1025. After his northern campaign he was given the title 'Gangaikonda' (bringer of the Ganga). He founded the new capital Gangaikonda Cholapuram, complete with a great temple. His empire stretched from the Bay of Bengal to the Maldives, and included coastal parts of Sri Lanka.

questions.stem: The 'Sangam' literature of ancient Tamilakam flourished under the patronage of:
questions.explanation: Sangam literature (~300 BCE to 300 CE) — assemblies of Tamil poets held at Madurai under the Pandyas, but also patronised by the Cholas and Cheras. Major works — Tolkappiyam (grammar), Ettutokai (Eight Anthologies), Pattuppattu (Ten Idylls), Silappatikaram (one of the five great epics). The tradition is a key source for the political, social and cultural life of early historic Tamilakam. along with Cheras and Cholas.
